achievement:
The achievement I'm proudest of is the AI safety benchmark I built at DS Digital Technology. A pharmaceutical client was developing an AI assistant to answer questions from patients with bone metastases, and they had no clear way to decide whether an answer was safe enough to show a patient. I worked with their clinical experts to turn that into something measurable: a set of 246 realistic patient questions and a six-part scoring rubric, including red-line rules for answers that must never be given. I then built a Python pipeline that sent the questions to six different AI models and scored more than 2,400 responses against the rubric.

The client adopted the benchmark as its official standard for accepting the product. It was meaningful to me because it wasn't just an analysis that sat in a report. It changed how decisions were made, and it was work where getting it right genuinely mattered for patients. It also taught me that the most important step in a project like this is agreeing with the experts what "good" looks like before building anything.
